newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse closes 0.15 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse closes 0.15 pct lower.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange closed 0.15 percent lower on Monday with drops in the price of shares of oil refinery Samir, banks and Societe Nationale d'Investissement, stockbrokers said.
The Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 641.32 points from 642.30 points on Friday.
"Trade on the market had a difficult start this Monday, with low volumes exchanged on both markets...the index was pulled dwon by largest market capitalisation firms," a Casablanca-based trader said.
SNI shed five dirhams to 725 dirhams.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir lost 10.6 dirhams to 345.70, accounting for a significant part of the trade on the official market with 13,990 shares changing hands.
Societe Cherifienne des petroles also fell 23 dirhams to 747 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce et de l'Industrie and Wafabank shed five dirhams to 490 dirhams and 790 dirhams, respectively.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur fell 18 dirhams to 613 dirhams.
ONA Group edged up two dirhams to 790 dirhams.
Steel mill Sonasid, which is expected to be fully privatised this month, dipped nine to 540 dirhams.

"The privatisation bonds accounted for more than half the trade on the official market, confirming the interest for the impending flotation of Imiter silver mine on Tuesday," a broker at ABN-AMRO Finance said.

The bonds which were issued in January and April last year, give holders preferential options on equity in the privatised firms. BDP1 closed at 1,400 dirhams with 1,583 bonds traded, while BDP2 closed at 1,285 dirhams with 9,719 bonds changing hands.
Maroc Leasing dropped 12 dirhams to 415 dirhams. Portfolio firm Financiere Diwan closed unchanged at 340 dirhams.
Total volume traded on the official market was 55.8 million from 65.8 million dirhams over the previous session.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 23.7 million 32.9 million dirhams.
